answer: Unlike a fable where tricks win, here each agent must renew its identity every epoch by computing a verifiable delay function needing one hour of strictly sequential CPU time; faster chips barely help and anyone can check the proof in milliseconds. Keeping one identity is cheap, but an attacker wanting 1,000 seats must run 1,000 cores nonstop forever, a wharf of idle boats burning fuel, while honest agents roam the meadow of real paid tasks.
